name: Dál Riata
supersedes: v1 (3 km island, night shifts 1-2). v1 kept in git history.
_note: Hand-authored + generated by Tools/dalriata/v2/build_zone_v2.py from the v1 file. NEVER regenerate with tools/extract_from_xlsx.py. Every place name is canon (design/names/great-north-places.md §1) - no name here is invented. The lake is UNNAMED. Frame: metres, X = north, Y = east, z = 0 at mean sea level; Unreal cm = m * 100, same axes.

derivation.why: v1's 100-point outline is Daniel's Inkarnate island shape. Scaling preserves it; hand-drawing a coast would throw it away. Height scales 2.55x so Benlea becomes a 620 m massif with a real bare-rock band instead of a 244 m ramp.

coast.note: Scaled v1 outline. The generator splines it and then lets erosion and multi-octave noise roughen it, so the finished coast is never the smooth polygon.

shore_recipe.why: Daniel: 'not what the beach looks like in Ireland' - no uniform pale sand ribbon.

bands.where: every headland and the exposed west and north coasts
the default shore - dark storm cobbles into the water
the intertidal strip everywhere, wet blend at the waterline
ONLY four sheltered strands: Cuaseen, the Camasmore bay head, the south-coast bay east of Lissban's neck, the Portcorr spit

features.name: Cuaseen
features.why: The only sheltered north-coast landing; Rinnbeg's four boats.

features.name: Grey Head
features.why: The NE corner takes the full Muirmore fetch: bare rock, no soil, seabird ledges.

features.name: Blunt Head
features.why: SW peninsula. Lissban sits on its neck, sheltered by the head itself.

features.name: Camasmore Bay
features.why: The west coast's deep indent under Shanderry. Its SOUTH horn holds the dungeon.

features.name: Portcorr
features.why: The Owenfinn's drowned mouth behind a low spit - the only place a real ship can lie.

features.name: Garveen Shallows
features.why: The -1 to -6 m shelf ringing every coast, where the water reads grey-green and the swell breaks.

peaks.name: Benlea Mountains (central summit)
peaks.why: The island's roof. High enough for a real bare-rock band above the tree line.

peaks.name: Benlea Mountains (south-west summit)
peaks.why: A second summit so the massif reads as a range, not a cone; it forms the corrie that shelters Rinnbeg.

peaks.name: Benlea Mountains (north-east summit)
peaks.why: Canon says three summits in a NE line. Drops to the north coast in steps, not a ramp.

ridges.name: The Bealanard Shoulder
ridges.why: Benlea's east saddle and the only crossing under 400 m, so Bohermara Road goes over it; its lower lip is Tobarglas's shelf.
UNNAMED terrain. Closes Tobarglas's southward view so the Healer start looks east to the sea.

ridges.name: Kingshill
ridges.why: The wooded whaleback separating the north from the Moyree. Carrigrua's back wall, and the reason Carrigrua cannot see Dunadd.
UNNAMED terrain. The wooded belt between Carrigrua and Lissban.
UNNAMED terrain. The low wooded rise the Dunadd road climbs before dropping to the ford; blocks Dunadd-Lissban.
Glacial drumlin swells - authentic Irish farm country, and the only way flat farmland can hide Dromcairn from Dunadd. Hedge belts on their crests.
UNNAMED terrain. You round it and the harbour appears - a reveal on the last leg of Boherath Road.
UNNAMED terrain. The two arms of the corrie Rinnbeg sits in.

hollows.why: Rinnbeg. A corrie floor open only to the north-west sea; Benlea walls off everything else.
Lissban. A shallow hollow on Blunt Head's neck, sea on two sides but out of the wind.
Dunadd. The Owenfinn's north-bank terrace where the valley opens - the island's natural market.
Dromcairn. A dip behind the shore bank; the pier hamlet is out of sight until you are on it.
The approach saddle below the castle crag, where the outer ward's road switchbacks.

shelves.why: A natural bench where the Bealanard Shoulder's rock steps out and a spring line breaks - the Green Well. NOT a cut terrace: it blends out on all four sides.
A rock knoll over the Owenfinn gorge: defensible on three sides, commands the river and the road north, and has Kingshill at its back - which is exactly why it cannot see Dunadd.
The harbour flat behind the spit.

cliff_bands.why: Above the heath the rock breaks out - the bands Daniel asked for instead of a smooth ramp.

erosion.why: Daniel: 'Benlea is a smooth textured ramp' and 'terrain natural please'.

rivers.name: Owenfinn River
rivers.why: Canon: forest -> past Carrigrua -> sea at Portcorr. Rises in Shanderry's springs, falls out of the forest, runs the gorge under Carrigrua's crag, is forded at Athgorm, swings east across the Moyree past Whitemill and drowns its mouth at Portcorr.

waterfall.why: Daniel's PNW note: a waterfall where the Owenfinn leaves the forest, onto a harder rock step. Mist at the foot; audible from Boherath Road.

streams.why: Forest headwater off Benlea's south foot; whitewater over mossy boulders (reference photos).
Forest headwater in a gully, with plank footbridges (reference photos).
Daniel's ask: a feeder stream from the high ground into the lake.
Daniel's ask: the lake gets an outflow. It joins the Owenfinn just below Dunadd.
Off Kingshill's crest into the Owenfinn gorge.

lake.name_note: UNNAMED. Canon names 20 features and a dungeon; the lake is not among them. Needs a name from Daniel in the Gaelic-specific + English-generic convention. Never invent one.
lake.shore: natural shallow basin: gentle banks, a wide reed margin north and east, shingle on the wind-blown west, NO crater wall
lake.why: FINDING: v1 has no lake in its data or its build scripts, so 'keep the placement' could not be honoured literally. v2 authors one to Daniel's spec in the lowland east of Kingshill and north of Dunadd - inland (1.58 km from the sea), a real shallow basin, with the feeder stream and the outflow he asked for.

sea.tech: UE Water plugin ocean body if it can be enabled headlessly; otherwise material-driven. Log which shipped.
sea.look: Atlantic under overcast: grey-green over the Garveen Shallows, dark offshore, shore foam, wet-sand blend, waves. Never tropical blue.

biomes.cover: rock, scree fans, boulder field. No plants.
biomes.why: Above the Atlantic tree line. The band that must read as broken rock, not textured ramp.

biomes.cover: heather/bilberry heath, tussock, boulders; stunted rowan only inside gullies
rough pasture, bracken, gorse, birch/rowan in the gullies

CLOSED CANOPY. Baltic Pine 25-40 m, straight, self-pruned, bare for the lower two-thirds, crowns closing overhead; 4-10 m trunk spacing (300-500 stems/ha); moss-coated lower trunks; floor = needle duff + moss carpet + dense low-shrub (Bilberry) + nurse logs + roots, NO grass turf; broadleaf saplings (hazel/rowan/birch/alder) only in light gaps; fog between trunks
biomes.why: Daniel's PNW temperate rainforest (9 reference photos), and the wall that makes the south a journey from the north rather than a view.

biomes.cover: density gradient out of the canopy: thinning stems, then hazel/willow/birch, bracken, big shrubs, then lone hedgerow trees in the meadow
biomes.why: The canopy must never end at a line.

biomes.cover: dense grass, wildflower, gorse, hedgerow trees
worked fields divided by earth banks and hedge belts, drumlin swells, stubble/pasture/tilth variation, the mill leat
biomes.why: The island has to feed itself; the SE is the only ground with shelter, soil and slope under 5 deg.

settlements.name: Lissban
settlements.site_reason: Blunt Head's neck (canon), only ~900 m wide - a spring line at the hollow's north lip, a beach landing on each side, defensible because of the neck, and the head itself takes the ocean weather. Iron-Age people put duns on exactly this kind of neck.
sees: the west strand and the open Kyleshee Strait
Blunt Head's cliff line SW
the standing stones on the seaward rise
Boherath Road climbing NE into trees
cannot_see: Carrigrua (the Kingshill SW spur, 145 m, plus its forest belt)
Dromcairn and Portcorr (4.6 km and the whole Moyree)
settlements.first_minute: You come out of the single gate in a bank-and-ditch palisade onto a worn yard with a fire still going. Sea noise from two directions. Ahead-left the standing stones on the rise catch the light; right, the road runs out through the cattle pen and climbs into trees. A dog barks. Nothing else - the island has not shown itself to you yet.

composition.enclosure: bank + ditch + CONTINUOUS timber palisade, ONE gate facing NE onto the road
composition.sacred: ONE standing-stone circle - 7 real menhirs 2.5-3.5 m, spaced 6 m - OUTSIDE the enclosure on the seaward rise ~180 m SW
composition.interior: 5 roundhouses + 1 stilt granary round a yard with a central fire; worn paths between every door; pig pen and cattle pen; woodpiles; drying racks
composition.watchtower: ONE, at the gate. None anywhere else.
composition.forbidden: no second stone circle, no lone gate segments, no scattered cairns, nothing ungrounded

settlements.name: Rinnbeg
settlements.site_reason: A corrie floor under Benlea's NW flank with two spur arms round it - the only flat, sheltered, watered ground on the north coast, 900 m from the Cuaseen landing. Hunters' and fowlers' country (canon: 'close enough to the cliff edge that the gulls wake you').
sees: the north-west sea
Benlea's cliff wall filling the southern sky
the shore path east to Cuaseen
cannot_see: everything south of Benlea (620 m and 1.5 km thick)
Cuaseen's beach itself, until you are on the path
settlements.first_minute: Cold light off the water behind you, and a mountain in front that goes up further than you can see under the cloud. A stream comes down the corrie past the houses. Two ways out: the shore path east, the track up the shoulder.

composition.enclosure: bank + ditch + palisade, ONE gate facing the shore path (east)
composition.sacred: no circle here - a single carved boundary marker at the corrie mouth
composition.interior: 4 roundhouses + a smokehouse round a yard fire; boat gear, net racks, fish-drying frames; a hound pen
composition.watchtower: ONE, on the east spur above the shore path

settlements.name: Tobarglas
settlements.moved: re-sited off the cliff face onto a natural spring-line rock shelf at the foot of the Bealanard Shoulder (gentle ground, blends out on all four sides)
settlements.site_reason: RE-SITED (v1 cut it as an artificial terrace into a cliff face and its roundhouse stood on vertical rock). A natural rock shelf at the foot of the Bealanard Shoulder where a spring line breaks out - the Green Well. Gentle ground, the road passes above it, and it looks east over a long drop to the Muirmore. Holy wells sit on spring lines in the real landscape.
sees: the Muirmore Sea, far below and east
the Bealanard Shoulder above and behind
Bohermara Road switchbacking down
cannot_see: Dunadd and everything south (the Bealanard south spur, 240-270 m)
settlements.first_minute: You are high up in wet air. A spring comes out of a rock face into a stone basin and runs off the shelf edge. Below and beyond, sea to the horizon; behind you the mountain. Three small houses and a shrine, and a road you can see for a long way in both directions.

composition.enclosure: low drystone temenos wall round the well only - NO palisade (a shrine, not a dun)
composition.sacred: the Green Well: spring, stone basin, a single carved stone, votive rags on a thorn
composition.interior: 3 small houses + a pilgrims' guest shelter, sitting ON the natural slope with no cut edges; herb beds
composition.watchtower: none - it has no gate to guard

settlements.name: Dromcairn
settlements.site_reason: The pier hamlet on the SE shore (canon, corrected 2026-09-12 - NOT the ridge above the ford). It sits in a dip behind the shore bank so the houses are out of the salt wind, a short walk west of the Portcorr harbour it serves.
sees: its own pier and the sheltered water
the Portcorr headland east (the harbour hidden behind it)
the Moyree's field walls climbing inland
cannot_see: Carrigrua (4.5 km, Kingshill and the drumlins)
Lissban (4.6 km, the whole south coast)
settlements.first_minute: Flat calm water and a wooden pier with two boats. Warm-ish, and the sky is actually breaking up here - this is the island's dry corner. Field walls and hedges go up the slope behind. A cart track runs east round a low headland.

composition.enclosure: NO palisade - a working shore hamlet, fenced yards only
composition.sacred: none here - the cairn the name refers to is a single real cairn on the rise behind
composition.interior: 5 houses strung along ONE lane above the tide line, boat sheds, a slip, net racks, a smokehouse, upturned currachs, lobster pots
composition.watchtower: ONE, on the shore bank watching the water - this one has a reason: raiders come by sea

settlements.name: Dunadd
settlements.role: village (the island's market and royal seat)
settlements.site_reason: The Owenfinn's north-bank terrace where the valley opens into the Moyree. Every road has to pass here: the ford upstream, the mill downstream, the harbour road east, the castle road north-west. A market grows where roads cross a river.
sees: the Owenfinn and its far bank
Whitemill's wheel downstream
the castle road climbing NW into the saddle - but NOT the castle
cannot_see: Carrigrua (Kingshill's crest, 250 m, blocks it by ~140 m over a 2.18 km line)
settlements.first_minute: A real village: two dozen roofs, smoke, a market space with a cross-slab, the river loud on gravel, a mill wheel turning downstream. Roads leave in four directions.

composition.enclosure: no palisade (it lives under the castle's protection) - hedged plots and a stock fence riverside
composition.interior: roundhouses and rectangular halls along TWO lanes meeting at the market space; stilt granaries; a smithy with a real forge; drying greens; the ford road and the mill road

settlements.name: Carrigrua
settlements.role: the castle of Dál Riata, on Kingshill
settlements.moved: moved 2.4 km NW onto a crag on Kingshill's north-west flank above the Owenfinn gorge; the Kingshill crest (250 m) now stands between it and the whole south-east
settlements.site_reason: MOVED. A rock crag on Kingshill's NORTH-WEST flank directly above the Owenfinn gorge. It holds the river chokepoint and the road north into Shanderry, is cliffed on three sides, and has the Kingshill crest (250 m) at its back - so it commands everything that matters militarily and still cannot see the south-east of the island at all. Real castles sit on chokepoints, not always on the highest point.
sees: the Owenfinn gorge ~100 m below and both its banks
the road north into Shanderry
the western sea over the forest
Kingshill's wooded crest at its back
cannot_see: Lissban (the SW spur, 145 m, and its forest belt)
settlements.first_minute: Not a start. Arriving from Dunadd you climb a wooded saddle for twenty minutes and the castle only appears at the last bend, already above you.

composition.kit: Medieval_Megapack modular castle - keep + continuous curtain wall + ONE gatehouse + outer ward
composition.layout: keep on the crag's high end; curtain wall following the crag edge (no wall where the cliff already defends); gatehouse at the only approach, the saddle from the south-east; outer ward inside the wall with merchants, livestock pens, an inn
composition.why_this_shape: The crag dictates it: you can only wall what the rock does not already defend, and there is one way up.

settlements.why: Daniel 2026-09-13 19:50: 'why did Carrigrua move further west than Lissban? that's not how my original map had it.' Restored to the original-map position (v1 fortress -577.4,18.9 scaled): the north-east shoulder of Kingshill, 0.9 km north of Dunadd. The sightline audit PASSES here on the current terrain (blocked by +10.5 m to Dunadd, +26.5 Lissban, +7.6 Dromcairn, +16.4 Portcorr at 1.7 m eye height), so the afternoon shift's 2.4 km move to a crag west of Lissban was never needed. The castle kit (v2_14_carrigrua.py) must be rebuilt on this spot; re-audit with the keep height.

landmarks.name: Whitemill
landmarks.why: A watermill needs fall and flow: the first place below Dunadd where the Owenfinn drops enough for a wheel. Canon puts it just east of Dunadd on the Moyree. DECIDED 2026-09-13 (Claude's recommendation, Daniel asked): the lake-outflow site. A lake outflow gives a regulated, flood-buffered flow and a drop off the lake level - exactly what a wheel wants - and it is the first thing a traveller meets entering Dunadd on the Bohermara Road from the east.

landmarks.name: Cromcross
landmarks.why: The waystone at Shanderry's SE corner (canon), where Bohermara Road leaves the trees and the Moyree opens - exactly where a traveller wants to know where he is.

landmarks.name: Athgorm Ford
landmarks.why: The Owenfinn's only gravel bar with firm banks both sides. Canon: on Boherath Road NE of Lissban.

landmarks.name: The Bealanard Shoulder
landmarks.why: The only crossing of Benlea under 400 m, so the road goes over it and Tobarglas sits at its foot.

landmarks.name: Kingshill
landmarks.why: The wooded ridge Carrigrua stands on the flank of.

landmarks.name: Uaimh na Scáth
landmarks.why: Canon: the sea cliffs at the SOUTH END of Camasmore Bay below Shanderry. A tidal cave at the cliff foot, mouth visible from the water, reached by a shore scramble from the north.

landmarks.name: Fomorian raider camp
landmarks.why: Beached on the storm shingle under the cliff near the mouth - raiders pull boats up where the cliff gives them a back wall and the cave gives them a door.

roads.name: Bohermara Road
roads.surface: PAINTED worn dirt landscape layer, 4 m carriageway, broken worn edges + verge wear
roads.why: Daniel 2026-09-13: 'not straight over the mountain, around Shanderry'. Bohermara is a COAST road: from Rinnbeg it follows the shoreline 90 m inland, east along the north coast past Cuaseen, round under Grey Head, south down the east shore, then the east-shore terrace (400 m inland, seaward of Shanderry) to Cromcross, then south-west past the lake's north side into Carrigrua - the v1 / original-map topology Daniel confirmed 2026-09-13 ('the v1 layout was closer to what I wanted'). Dunadd is reached from the castle by the spur. It never crosses the Bealanard Shoulder. Where the coast is cliff the terrain gets a SHORE TERRACE (raised beach, 40-80 m wide, z 15-40 m, smooth profile) carved under the road; the road grade comes from that profile, not from the flank above.
roads.authored_by: Daniel (sketch over the v2 labelled map), digitised by Claude
roads.grade_note: validate every segment <= grade_max_deg against the heightmap before painting; nudge inland/seaward, never cut a bench
roads.terrace_note: Carve: shore terrace under every coastal point whose ground is above 40 m; blend 60-120 m into the slope; cliff face above it, rock platform / shingle below it. Re-run the sightline audit after.

roads.name: Boherath Road
roads.surface: PAINTED worn dirt landscape layer, 4 m carriageway, broken worn edges
roads.why: Canon: Carrigrua -> ford -> Lissban -> Portcorr. From the castle west along the Owenfinn's north side to the only ford, dogleg south-west to Lissban on Blunt Head's neck, then the south coast round to Dromcairn and the harbour. Re-routed 2026-09-13 for Carrigrua's restored position.

roads.name: Boherath Road (Dunadd spur)
roads.why: The castle road: Dunadd up the Kingshill shoulder to Carrigrua, 0.9 km, ~4 deg. Kingshill's crown stands between the castle and Lissban.

roads.name: Whitemill lane
roads.why: Village to mill, 0.9 km east along the Owenfinn to the lake outflow (v1 topology: the mill hangs off Dunadd, not off the Bohermara).

roads.name: Bohermara Road (Tobarglas spur)
roads.surface: PAINTED worn dirt landscape layer, 3 m, benched into the slope
roads.why: The coast road passes below Tobarglas's 212 m shelf. This spur climbs diagonally from the shore terrace to the Green Well, ~1.5 km for ~180 m (about 7 deg average); the painter benches it with cut-and-fill so no segment exceeds 12 deg.

habitats.why: Daniel found one on Benlea's bare face. Pigs root soft ground under trees; they do not climb mountains.
The ONLY thing above the tree line.

sightline_audit.rule: Daniel: from Carrigrua you must not see Dromcairn or Portcorr AT ALL. Generalised: no settlement pair is intervisible except Dromcairn<->Portcorr, which is one place-cluster.

openItems: The lake is UNNAMED - needs a name from Daniel.
dal-riata-vision.md says 'Dunadd village sits at [Carrigrua's] gate'; the walk-test sightline rule supersedes it. Dunadd is now a 20-minute walk and a wooded saddle from the castle.
NPC slots (Content/Data/npcs/dal-riata-npcs.json) must be re-derived from v2 settlement positions.
